title: The product's own in-page card feed shape, as a bare single object, is untyped

source.name: ortbtools knowledge base — in-page native widget card
source.notes: Field shape (id/title/text/image/icon/clickurl/impurl/advertiser/price/currency/ext.format+widget_id+zone_id) is the product's own documented in-page widget card sample, reproduced here as a bare single object instead of the KB file's one-element array.

modifications: Card id, image/click/impression URLs and advertiser domain independently authored; the KB sample's cdn.example/click.example/imp.example hosts replaced with this corpus's assets/advertiser/tracking.example.test convention.
Presented as a bare object rather than the KB file's `[{...}]` wrapper, to isolate the single-object-vs-array behaviour difference.
provenance.sanitized: No real advertiser or subscriber data; all hosts are reserved .test domains; price is a small synthetic placeholder.

response.title: A quiet morning by the lake
response.text: Compare three original travel-planning tools before you book.

specNotes: packages/core/detect.js looksLikeJsonFeedSingle() only accepts click_url|link as the click-key half of its price+click+creative co-occurrence test (and clickUrl/notification_url/bid_price/redirecturl for the other single-object shapes); this card's `clickurl` (no separator) satisfies none of them, so detectType() falls through to TYPES.UNKNOWN and the top-level validator reports payload.unknown_type.

packages/core/format-detect.js detectFeedFormat() is a separate function from detectType(); its hasClick set explicitly includes clickurl (alongside clickUrl/click_url/redirectUrl/link), so it correctly tags FORMATS.INPAGE for this exact object even while detectType() cannot name a payload type for it at all — the format-tagging and payload-typing layers disagree about whether this shape is recognised.

This is the product's own committed knowledge_base/jsonfeed/inpage/inpage-card.json sample (manifest id kb-jsonfeed-inpage-001), reproduced as a bare object; the KB file itself only ships the one-element-array form, so the single-object form of its own reference shape was never previously exercised anywhere in the repo.
notes: No request side exists for this scenario: the KB shape has no documented paired BidRequest, and inventing an OpenRTB request for a feed-only material would not reflect any real wire contract.

preview.capabilityGap: findPushMaterial()'s isMat() test requires click_url or link; this card's clickurl key satisfies neither, so the front-end never recognises it as a push-style material and shows the empty state instead of a card, matching the same clickurl-alias gap as the Core validator.
